pr_title: Fixes the exception message handling to return the python dll name
pr_body:
#### Description
Do not rely on `string.GetStringBetweenChars` to get the python dll name, because it is not bound by the same chars in Windows and Unix systems. Instead use 'python' string and limits the dll name to 10 characters.

#### Related Issue
Closes #2164 

#### Motivation and Context
Improve error messages.

#### Requires Documentation Change
No.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
Running Lean in both Windows and Linux (docker).

issue_context.title: Missing information in DllNotFoundPythonExceptionInterpreter for Linux
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
The `DllNotFoundPythonExceptionInterpreter` message should read:
```
The dynamic-link library for python36 could not be found. Please visit https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Algorithm.Python/readme.md for instructions on how to enable python support in Unix
```
Note **python36**

#### Actual Behavior
The `DllNotFoundPythonExceptionInterpreter` message reads:
```
The dynamic-link library for  could not be found. Please visit https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Algorithm.Python/readme.md for instructions on how to enable python support in Unix
```
See #1746 messages from users.

#### Potential Solution
It looks like that a `DllNotFoundException` message does not have `'` `'`, `therefore string.GetStringBetweenChars` returns an empty string.

#### Reproducing the Problem
Run Lean in Linux with Python.Runtime.dll compiled for Windows.

#### System Information
Linux.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue

review_comments:
I believe it's possible that `DllNotFoundException` is thrown and have it not be related to python, so we should be careful here and expect strings that don't meet the pattern we expect. For example, we should handle 
```
if (startIndex < 0) // not python, emit a different message
```

In your tests, did you notice if the original message made it to the log file?

`DllNotFoundPythonExceptionInterpreter.CanInterpret` is only true if the exception message contains `python`, so `startIndex` is always greater than `-1`.

Yes, the original message makes to the log file.
Here is the message from the user in #1746:
> 20180322 19:51:24.602 ERROR:: Loader.TryCreatePythonAlgorithm(): System.Exception: AlgorithmPythonWrapper(): The dynamic-link library for could not be found. Please visit https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Algorithm.Python/readme.md for instructions on how to enable python support in Unix python3.6

The original message is **python3.6** in the end.
awesome, love seeing the infrastructure working hard!
So long as we're logging the full, original message, then this works for me.
